test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 9 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which part of the Constitution of India has been influenced by the German Constitution?

options.text: Suspension of fundamental rights during Emergency

solution:
The correct answer is the __**Suspension of fundamental rights during Emergency**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Suspension of Fundamental Rights

 
 
• The feature of suspending Fundamental Rights during an Emergency was taken from the Weimar Constitution of Germany
 
 
 
• **Articles 352–360 :**
 
 
• These articles in Part XVIII of the Constitution outline the Emergency provisions.. 
 
 
 
• **National, State, and Financial Emergencies**
 
 
• **The Indian Constitution, like the German Constitution, has provisions for national and state emergencies, as well as financial emergencies. **
 
 
 
• The Indian Constitution was also influenced by other sources, including:
 
 
• The Nehru Report and the Cabinet Mission Plan
 
• The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
 
• Principles of natural justice
 
• Parliamentary debates
 
• Judicial decisions
 
• Conventions 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Single citizenship**

 
 
• The **concept of single citizenship in India was inspired by the British Constitution, and the procedure for amending the Constitution was adopted from the South African Constitution**
 
 
 
• **Federal System in India:**
 
 
• **​**India follows a **federal system of governance, as outlined in the Constitution of India.**
 
• This system is a balance between a strong central government and regional or state governments.
 
• The federal system in India is **quasi-federal, meaning it is not a true federation like the United States** but has features that resemble a federal structure with a strong central authority.
 
 
 
• **Amendment of the Constitution of India:**
 
 
• **​**The **Constitution of India is a living document**, which means it can be amended to address changing circumstances.
 
• **Article 368 of the Constitution deals with the process of amendments.**
 
• The procedure to amend the Constitution is not simple and varies based on the nature of the amendment.
 
 

1c
